podcast.title: "Oh, You Pretty Thing" Article (January 22, 1972)
podcast.body: This British music weekly published a front-page article in its January 22, 1972 issue titled "Oh, You Pretty Thing," featuring David Bowie. The article detailed Bowie's effeminate, camp image and his use of sexual ambiguity, which was seen as a deliberate act of "shocking outrage" for pop music. "He gave an interview to Melody Maker, one of the big British music weeklies. The title of the article was, oh, you pretty thing."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Surprising History of Glam Rock

podcast.title: Calling Vince Clarke "The Messiah of Pop"
podcast.body: The music publication Melody Maker bestowed the title "the messiah of pop" upon Vince Clarke in the 1980s, recognizing his consistent and significant contributions to popular music through his various successful projects during that decade. "Melody Maker lo llamaba el mesías, el poco en la época de los 80."

podcast.title: Melody Maker's Role in Britpop
podcast.body: The weekly music paper Melody Maker, alongside NME, played a part in promoting Britpop by covering what appeared to be a "new and very viable local music scene." "And the weekly papers, the NME and Melodymaker, some thirtieth into what appeared to be a new and very viable local music scene."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The Rise and Fall of Britpop

podcast.title: Role in British Music Press
podcast.body: Melody Maker was an influential British music magazine that, in the absence of widespread commercial radio, took on the role of discovering new music, building up bands, and providing exposure. "The NME, sounds, melody maker, and dozens more filled the gap played by radio in North America."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
